title: Equivalent Fractions
seo_title: Grade 5 Equivalent Fractions Worksheets (BC Curriculum) – Free with Answer Key
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 math worksheets on equivalent fractions for the BC curriculum: fraction bars, fraction walls and number lines, multiplying and dividing the numerator and denominator, simplest form, comparing fractions, and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Equivalent fractions: multiply or divide the top and the bottom by the same number.
key_sub: 3/4 = 9/12 (× 3) and 8/12 = 2/3 (÷ 4). Never add the same number to both: 2/3 is not 4/5. To compare, use a common denominator: 3/5 = 6/10 < 7/10.
body_html:
Equivalent fractions

Equivalent fractions show the same amount of the same whole. To find one, multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number. The parts get smaller, but there are more of them.

Example

34 = ?12

4 × 3 = 12, so multiply the numerator by 3 too: 3 × 3 = 9.

Answer: 912

A number line shows the same idea. 23 and 46 are at the same point.

Dividing and simplest form

You can also divide the numerator and the denominator by the same number. A fraction is in simplest form when no number except 1 divides both. Divide by the greatest number you can.

Example

Write 812 in simplest form.

4 divides both 8 and 12. 8 ÷ 4 = 2 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3.

Answer: 23

Comparing fractions

Write the fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators. If the numerators are the same, the fraction with the smaller denominator is greater, because its parts are bigger.

Example

Which is greater: 35 or 710?

Use tenths: 35 = 610. 7 tenths is more than 6 tenths.

Answer: 710

Example

Order 34, 58 and 12 from least to greatest.

Use eighths: 34 = 68, 58, 12 = 48.

Answer: 12, 58, 34

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the same number to the top and bottom: 23 = 45Multiply or divide, never add: 23 = 46
Multiplying only the numerator: 23 = 43Multiply both: 23 = 46
Stopping too early: 1218 = 69Keep going, or divide by the greatest common factor: 1218 = 23
Thinking a bigger denominator means a bigger fraction: 18 > 14A bigger denominator means smaller parts: 18 < 14

faq.q: What do Grade 5 students learn about fractions in BC?
faq.a: In the BC Grade 5 math curriculum, students work with equivalent fractions. They use models such as fraction bars and number lines, find equivalent fractions by multiplying or dividing, write fractions in simplest form, and compare fractions.

faq.q: How do you find an equivalent fraction?
faq.a: Multiply or divide the numerator and the denominator by the same number. For example, 3/4 = 9/12 (both × 3) and 8/12 = 2/3 (both ÷ 4). Adding the same number to both does not work: 2/3 is not equal to 4/5.

faq.q: How do you write a fraction in simplest form?
faq.a: Find the greatest number that divides both the numerator and the denominator, and divide both by it. For 12/18, divide by 6 to get 2/3. If you divide by a smaller number first, keep going until only 1 divides both.

faq.q: How do you compare fractions with different denominators?
faq.a: Write both fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators. For 3/5 and 7/10, 3/5 = 6/10, so 7/10 is greater.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 34 is shaded. How many eighths are equal to 34?
items.e: Look down the fraction wall. Each fourth is the same as 2 eighths, so 3 fourths line up with 3 × 2 = 6 eighths. So 34 = 68.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 23 is shaded. How many twelfths are equal to 23?
items.e: Look down the fraction wall. Each third is the same as 4 twelfths, so 2 thirds line up with 2 × 4 = 8 twelfths. So 23 = 812.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 45 is shaded. How many tenths are equal to 45?
items.e: Look down the fraction wall. Each fifth is the same as 2 tenths, so 4 fifths line up with 4 × 2 = 8 tenths. So 45 = 810.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 56 is shaded. How many twelfths are equal to 56?
items.e: Look down the fraction wall. Each sixth is the same as 2 twelfths, so 5 sixths line up with 5 × 2 = 10 twelfths. So 56 = 1012.

items.q: The arrow points to 34 on the top line. Which fraction on the bottom line is at the same point?
items.e: The bottom line is split into eighths, so each fourth on the top line is 2 eighths. Count 3 × 2 = 6 marks from 0 on the bottom line. So 34 = 68.

items.q: The arrow points to 23 on the top line. Which fraction on the bottom line is at the same point?
items.e: The bottom line is split into sixths, so each third on the top line is 2 sixths. Count 2 × 2 = 4 marks from 0 on the bottom line. So 23 = 46.

items.q: The arrow points to 25 on the top line. Which fraction on the bottom line is at the same point?
items.e: The bottom line is split into tenths, so each fifth on the top line is 2 tenths. Count 2 × 2 = 4 marks from 0 on the bottom line. So 25 = 410.

items.q: The arrow points to 14 on the top line. Which fraction on the bottom line is at the same point?
items.e: The bottom line is split into twelfths, so each fourth on the top line is 3 twelfths. Count 1 × 3 = 3 marks from 0 on the bottom line. So 14 = 312.

items.q: 912 of the bar is shaded. The thick lines make groups of 3 parts. Which equivalent fraction does the bar show?
items.e: There are 4 groups and 3 of them are shaded, so 912 = 34. This is the same as dividing 9 and 12 by 3.

items.q: 610 of the bar is shaded. The thick lines make groups of 2 parts. Which equivalent fraction does the bar show?
items.e: There are 5 groups and 3 of them are shaded, so 610 = 35. This is the same as dividing 6 and 10 by 2.

items.q: 812 of the bar is shaded. The thick lines make groups of 4 parts. Which equivalent fraction does the bar show?
items.e: There are 3 groups and 2 of them are shaded, so 812 = 23. This is the same as dividing 8 and 12 by 4.

items.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 25?
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 3: 2 × 3 = 6 and 5 × 3 = 15. So 25 = 615. 69 adds 4 to both numbers, so it is a different amount.

items.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 34?
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 5: 3 × 5 = 15 and 4 × 5 = 20. So 34 = 1520. 56 adds 2 to both numbers, so it is a different amount.

items.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 49?
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 2: 4 × 2 = 8 and 9 × 2 = 18. So 49 = 818. 712 adds 3 to both numbers, so it is a different amount.

items.q: Which fraction is not equivalent to 35?
items.e: 57 is not equivalent to 35: 2 was added to the numerator and the denominator, and adding changes the amount. The others are equivalent, because both numbers were multiplied by the same number.

items.q: Which fraction is not equivalent to 34?
items.e: 67 is not equivalent to 34: 3 was added to the numerator and the denominator, and adding changes the amount. The others are equivalent, because both numbers were multiplied by the same number.

items.q: Which pair of fractions is equivalent?

34 and 56
13 and 29
46 and 1015
items.e: Simplify both: 46 = 23 and 1015 = 23. They are the same, so 46 and 1015 are equivalent. In the other pairs the two fractions show different amounts.

items.q: Which fraction is in simplest form?
items.e: 58 is in simplest form, because no number except 1 divides both 5 and 8. The others can be simplified: 46 = 23, 610 = 35, 39 = 13.

items.q: Which fraction is in simplest form?
items.e: 712 is in simplest form, because no number except 1 divides both 7 and 12. The others can be simplified: 912 = 34, 210 = 15, 48 = 12.

items.q: Which fraction is in simplest form?
items.e: 49 is in simplest form, because no number except 1 divides both 4 and 9. The others can be simplified: 615 = 25, 1012 = 56, 312 = 14.

items.q: To write 1218 in simplest form, Kai divides the numerator and the denominator by the greatest number that divides both. What is that number?
items.e: Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. The greatest number in both lists is 6. 2 and 3 also divide both, but 6 is greater. So 1218 = 23.

items.q: To write 1624 in simplest form, Kai divides the numerator and the denominator by the greatest number that divides both. What is that number?
items.e: Factors of 16: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. The greatest number in both lists is 8. 2 and 4 also divide both, but 8 is greater. So 1624 = 23.

items.q: Write 68 in simplest form.
items.e: 2 is the greatest number that divides both 6 and 8. 6 ÷ 2 = 3 and 8 ÷ 2 = 4. So 68 = 34.

items.q: Write 410 in simplest form.
items.e: 2 is the greatest number that divides both 4 and 10. 4 ÷ 2 = 2 and 10 ÷ 2 = 5. So 410 = 25.

items.q: Write 39 in simplest form.

items.q: Write 515 in simplest form.
items.e: 5 is the greatest number that divides both 5 and 15. 5 ÷ 5 = 1 and 15 ÷ 5 = 3. So 515 = 13.

items.e: 3 is the greatest number that divides both 9 and 12. 9 ÷ 3 = 3 and 12 ÷ 3 = 4. So 912 = 34.

items.q: Write 1015 in simplest form.

items.q: Write 1624 in simplest form.

items.q: Write 1824 in simplest form.

items.q: Harjot writes 1218 in simplest form as 69. Is he right?

No. It is 35
items.e: 5 divides both 15 and 20: 15 ÷ 5 = 3 and 20 ÷ 5 = 4. 3 and 4 have no common factor except 1, so 34 is the simplest form. Mei is right.

items.q: Which is greater: 38 or 35?
items.e: The numerators are the same, so compare the size of the parts. Eighths are smaller than fifths, because the whole is cut into more parts. So 35 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 29 or 27?
items.e: The numerators are the same, so compare the size of the parts. Ninths are smaller than sevenths, because the whole is cut into more parts. So 27 is greater.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which is greater: 23 or 712?
items.e: Use twelfths for both: 23 = 812 and 712. 8 > 7, so 23 is greater.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which is greater: 58 or 34?
items.e: Use eighths for both: 58 and 34 = 68. 6 > 5, so 34 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 35 or 710?
items.e: Use tenths for both: 35 = 610 and 710. 7 > 6, so 710 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 56 or 1112?
items.e: Use twelfths for both: 56 = 1012 and 1112. 11 > 10, so 1112 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 34 or 912?
items.e: Use twelfths for both: 34 = 912 and 912. The numerators are the same, so they are equal.

items.q: Which is greater: 12 or 512?
items.e: Use twelfths for both: 12 = 612 and 512. 6 > 5, so 12 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 23 or 34?
items.e: Use twelfths for both: 23 = 812 and 34 = 912. 9 > 8, so 34 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 45 or 710?
items.e: Use tenths for both: 45 = 810 and 710. 8 > 7, so 45 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 25 or 13?
items.e: Use fifteenths for both: 25 = 615 and 13 = 515. 6 > 5, so 25 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 58 or 23?
items.e: Use twenty-fourths for both: 58 = 1524 and 23 = 1624. 16 > 15, so 23 is greater.

items.q: To compare 23 and 34, Lucas writes both with the same denominator. Which denominator works?
items.e: The denominator must be a multiple of both 3 and 4. 12 is: 3 × 4 = 12. So 23 = 812 and 34 = 912. 7 = 3 + 4 does not work: you can’t make sevenths from thirds or fourths.

items.q:

items.e: Write them all with the denominator 8: 34 = 68, 58, 12 = 48, 38. The greatest is 68, so the answer is 34.

items.q:

items.q:

35, 710, 12, 25
items.e: Write them all with the denominator 10: 35 = 610, 710, 12 = 510, 25 = 410. The greatest is 710, so the answer is 710.

c: 12, 310, 25
310, 12, 25

items.e: Use the denominator 10: 310, 12 = 510, 25 = 410. So the order is 12, 25, 310.

items.q: Which fraction is between 12 and 34?
items.e: In eighths: 12 = 48 and 34 = 68. 58 is between them. 38 is less than 12. 78 and 56 are more than 34.

items.q: Which fraction is between 13 and 12?
items.e: In twelfths: 13 = 412 and 12 = 612. 512 is between them. 14 = 312 is too small. 712 and 23 = 812 are too big.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Liam eats 34 of the pizza. How many slices does he eat?
items.e: 4 × 2 = 8, so multiply the top by 2 too: 34 = 68. Liam eats 6 slices.

items.q: A muffin recipe needs 23 cup of milk. Ava’s measuring cup is marked in sixths. How many sixths of a cup should she pour?
items.e: 3 × 2 = 6, so multiply the top by 2 too: 23 = 46. Ava pours 4 sixths of a cup.

items.q: On a field trip to a salmon hatchery, Mei counts 12 fish in a tank. 8 of them are coho salmon. What fraction of the fish are coho, in simplest form?
items.e: 8 out of 12 is 812. 4 divides both: 8 ÷ 4 = 2 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3. So 23 of the fish are coho.

items.q: In the Terry Fox Run, Ethan has run 35 of the route. Nadia has run 710 of the same route. Who has run farther?
c: They have run the same distance
items.e: Use tenths: 35 = 610. 7 tenths is more than 6 tenths, so Nadia has run farther.

items.q: A BC Ferries boat has gone 68 of the way to Nanaimo. Kai says that is 34 of the way. Is he right?
c: No. 68 = 46
No. 34 is less than 68
Yes. 68 = 34
No. 68 = 24
items.e: Divide the top and the bottom of 68 by 2: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 and 8 ÷ 2 = 4. So 68 = 34. Kai is right.

items.q: Liam’s class plants 20 cedar seedlings. After a month, 15 of them are taller than 10 cm. What fraction of the seedlings are taller than 10 cm, in simplest form?
items.e: 15 out of 20 is 1520. 5 divides both: 15 ÷ 5 = 3 and 20 ÷ 5 = 4. So 34. (1318 takes 2 from both, which changes the amount.)

items.q: Owen says, “16 is greater than 13, because 6 is greater than 3.” Is he right?
c: Yes. Sixths are bigger than thirds
No. 16 is less than 13
items.e: A bigger denominator means the whole is cut into more, smaller parts. 13 = 26, which is more than 16. So 16 is less than 13.

items.q: Simran wants a fraction equivalent to 35. She writes 57. What did she do wrong?
c: She added 2 to the top and the bottom
items.e: 3 + 2 = 5 and 5 + 2 = 7. Adding changes the amount. Multiply both numbers by 2 instead: 35 = 610.

items.q: In a lacrosse game, Olivia scored on 4 of her 10 shots. Zara scored on 3 of her 5 shots. Who scored on a greater fraction of her shots?
items.e: Olivia: 410. Zara: 35 = 610. 6 tenths is more than 4 tenths, so Zara scored on a greater fraction.

items.q: On a hike in Stanley Park, Lucas has walked 56 of a trail. Jasleen has walked 34 of the same trail. Who has walked farther?
c: They have walked the same distance
items.e: Use twelfths: 56 = 1012 and 34 = 912. 10 twelfths is more than 9 twelfths, so Lucas has walked farther.

items.q: It rained in Vancouver on 18 of the 30 days in November. What fraction of the days had rain, in simplest form?
items.e: 18 out of 30 is 1830. 6 divides both: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 and 30 ÷ 6 = 5. So 35 of the days had rain.

items.q: Four students cut ribbons for a class project. Mateo: 34 m. Hana: 78 m. Kai: 58 m. Sofia: 12 m. Who has the longest ribbon?
items.e: Use eighths: 34 = 68, 78, 58, 12 = 48. The longest is Hana’s ribbon.

items.q: Two pizzas are the same size. One is cut into 6 equal slices and the other into 12. Noah eats 2 slices of the first pizza. How many slices of the second pizza must Leah eat to eat the same amount?
items.e: Noah eats 26. 6 × 2 = 12, so multiply the top by 2 too: 26 = 412. Leah must eat 4 slices.

items.q: At a ski hill near Kelowna, 10 of the 16 runs are open. What fraction of the runs are open, in simplest form?
items.e: 10 out of 16 is 1016. 2 divides both: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 and 16 ÷ 2 = 8. 5 and 8 have no other common factor, so 58 of the runs are open.

items.q: A whale-watching boat near Victoria sees 12 orcas. 4 of them are calves. Ji-woo writes 412 for the fraction that are calves. Which fraction is equivalent to 412?
items.e: Divide the top and the bottom of 412 by 2: 4 ÷ 2 = 2 and 12 ÷ 2 = 6. So 412 = 26 (and also 13).

items.q: Three groups each have the same size pot of paint for a mural. Group A uses 56 of its pot, Group B uses 712 and Group C uses 23. Which group uses the least paint?
items.e: Use twelfths: 56 = 1012, 712, 23 = 812. The smallest is 712, so Group B uses the least. 12 is the biggest denominator, but that does not make it the biggest fraction.

items.q: The school soccer team won 6 of its 8 games. The lacrosse team won 9 of its 12 games. Which team won a greater fraction of its games?
items.e: Soccer: 68 = 34. Lacrosse: 912 = 34. Both are 34, so they won the same fraction.

items.q: On a family trip along the Sea-to-Sky Highway, Jasleen says they have driven more than 12 but less than 34 of the way. Which fraction could it be?
items.e: In eighths: 12 = 48 and 34 = 68. Only 58 is between them. 56 = 1012 is more than 34.

items.q: Wei has read 15 of the 20 pages in his story. Harjot has read the same fraction of a story with 8 pages. How many pages has Harjot read?
items.e: 1520 = 34 (divide both by 5). Then 34 = 68 (multiply both by 2). Harjot has read 6 pages.

items.q: Sofia gets 1820 on a math quiz. Ryan gets 810 on a different quiz. Who got the greater fraction of the questions right?
items.e: Simplify Sofia’s score: 1820 = 910 (divide both by 2). 9 tenths is more than 8 tenths, so Sofia got the greater fraction right.
